title: Can any warp drive move a payload without negative energy?
question: Can any warp-drive spacetime move a payload faster than light, or at all, without negative energy? Weigh the Alcubierre and Natário metrics against the positive-energy and subluminal solutions proposed since 2020 (Lentz, Fell–Heisenberg, Bobrick–Martire, and the 2024 constant-velocity "physical war…
bottom_line: No. Under established physics no warp spacetime carries a payload faster than light without negative energy, meaning a violation of the null energy condition (non-negative energy along every light ray). For the Alcubierre, Natário, Lentz and Fell–Heisenberg family this is a theorem, confirmed here by direct calculation; for massive positive-energy shells the allowed internal "shift" stays 3 to 80 times below what even interior superluminality needs. Confidence about 94%. The 2024 positive-energy shell does pass all four energy conditions at its published setting, but it is a coasting Jupiter-mass shell, not a drive: it moves only as any massive vehicle does, and its one invariant "warp" signature is a 7-nanosecond light-timing asymmetry. Building it lies 22–28 orders of magnitude beyond demonstrated capability.
